# Voter-roll chapter: research (collected 2026-11-13, draft)

## 1. Names removed
- **130 million+** is accurate as reported, but it is a cumulative *draft-roll* deletion count across Bihar, Phase 2 (12 States/UTs) and Phase 3 drafts (still ongoing). Not a final-roll net change.
- Al Jazeera 8 Oct 2026 (AP/Reuters): "India's Election Commission has so far removed more than 130 million names from the voter lists" (verified).
- Reuters explainer 9 Oct: "Election Commission data cited by Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party shows about 130 million names". The claimant is the BJP citing ECI data. No ECI press note with a national total found.
- NYT (via Boston Globe, 6 Oct): "more than 130 million names". HRW 28 Oct: "over 130 million names".
- More recent/other: Outlook 3 Sep: estimated 13.37 crore, about 14.1% of pre-SIR rolls, 30 States/UTs (draft, unsourced estimate). Deccan Herald "13.3 crore" (403, unconfirmed).
- Final rolls: nearly six crore for Bihar + Phase 2 (PTI/Deccan Chronicle); Bihar 7.89 to 7.42 crore; Phase 2 50.99 to 45.81 crore. SabrangIndia: 61.38 to 55.17 crore (about 6.21 crore net).
- Scope: Bihar (Jun-Sep 2025), Phase 2 (UP, WB, TN, Gujarat, MP, Rajasthan, Chhattisgarh, Kerala, Goa, Puducherry, A&N, Lakshadweep), Phase 3 (16 States + 3 UTs, 36.73 crore electors; Himachal, J&K deferred, Assam awaits NRC).

## 2. Denominator
- ECI: 96,88,21,926 registered electors as of 8 Feb 2024 (announced 9 Feb 2024; via news summaries, ECI press note not fetched). NYT: "about 970 million". Reuters: "nearly one billion". HRW says 960M (outlier).
- Phase electorates: 7.89 + 50.99 + 36.73 = 95.61 crore (includes undrafted Phase 3 states). Outlook's 14.1% implies about 94.8 crore.
- Valid? Yes, nearly nationwide, so national division is defensible. 130/968.8 = 13.4; 133.7/about 95 = 14.0-14.1.
- **Recommendation:** "about 13 in every 100" survives for draft-stage deletions "so far", attributed "reported" (BJP citing ECI data). Mention that final rolls net about 6 crore (about 10 per 100) for Bihar + Phase 2, Phase 3 pending. Scale view: 9,690 marks, 1,300 removed is arithmetically consistent (968.8M / 100k, 130M / 100k).

## 3. Commission's reasons
Reuters: names "only removed" when a voter has died, is mentioned more than once, has moved or is untraceable. PIB (unverified, 403): death, permanent shifting, duplicates, untraceable after repeated visits; no deletion without hearing and written order by ERO. Only breakdown found is the BJP's (28M dead, 63M relocated, 10M duplicates, 30M untraceable; sums 131M). Bihar (PIB, summary): 18 lakh dead, 26 lakh shifted, 7 lakh duplicates.

## 4. Commissioners
Indian Express investigation (Ritika Chopra, 23 Sep 2026): Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi formally objected at least 14 times in about 10 months. ECI officials: "all decisions ... were unanimous". Al Jazeera 2 Oct snippet is verified. IE original not fetched.

## 5. Counter-figures
HRW (West Bengal): about 93% of decided appeals restored. Yadav (SC, 28 Jan 2026): 2.97 lakh Bihar names reappeared vs ECI 36,475. ADR apprehended nearly 3 crore disenfranchised (2025, via Wikipedia). Yadav/Wire projection of about 15 crore "missing" is an estimate. SC May 2026: data did not show "systemic disenfranchisement" (per HRW); upheld SIR.

## Conflicts
130M (draft) vs about 6 crore (final); 13.3/13.37 crore vs 130M (rounding); 960M (HRW) vs 968.8M (ECI); 63M relocated + 30M untraceable (BJP) vs Deccan Herald's 71.5% combined; HRW's 93% restored is Bengal-only.

## Fetch failures
403: Deccan Herald, Business Standard, PIB, The Statesman. ECI primary pages not retrieved. Quotes marked verified=false came from fetch summaries, not verbatim; confirm before on-screen use.
